answer:
At 10 bar(a), ammonia's latent heat of vaporisation is about 1166 kJ/kg, or about 19.9 kJ/mol using M = 17.03 g/mol. Its saturation temperature at that pressure is about 298.06 K (24.9 °C).

I calculated this with CoolProp, which uses the Helmholtz-energy equation of state for ammonia (Gao et al. 2020 in current versions). I took the difference between the enthalpies of saturated vapour and saturated liquid at 10 bar(a): h_vap − h_liq = 1166.18 kJ/kg.

I did not check the number against a second independent source in this session. From memory, standard ammonia tables give about 1166 kJ/kg at 25 °C, which agrees, but that is a recollection and was not computed here.

tools.name: Bash
tools.input:
{"command": "python3 -c "
import CoolProp.CoolProp as CP
P=10e5
T=CP.PropsSI('T','P',P,'Q',0,'Ammonia')
hv=CP.PropsSI('H','P',P,'Q',1,'Ammonia');hl=CP.PropsSI('H','P',P,'Q',0,'Ammonia')
print(T,T-273.15,(hv-hl)/1e3)
" 2>&1 || pip install -q CoolProp 2>&1 | tail -1", "description": "Compute ammonia latent heat at 10 bar with CoolProp"}
